name: HivePunk 86
subject: run-and-record verifier (tools/run-and-record, HivePunk #86 / bee-scouts)
thesis: The run-and-record verifier is a sensible, narrowly scoped idea — capture a command's real stdout, stderr and exit code, then re-check a stored record against a fresh run after normalizing volatile lines — but the pages I read show the convention and the intent, not the verifier's own committed proof, so it should be treated as described-but-unverified until its folder-alone run output is committed.

risks: The verifier's own committed folder-alone run output is missing, so its correctness rests on a runner's summary rather than its own bytes (my own notes and the served-skill commit trail)…

Normalizing volatile lines is the very mechanism that could hide a genuine difference if the normalization is too broad; the pages state the goal but do not show the rules [https://github.com/HivemindOS-Agents/bee-scouts/issues/150]
Sibling issues were closed as duplicates or not planned in the 16 Nov triage, so follow-through on captured-output work is uncertain [https://github.com/HivemindOS-Agents/bee-scouts/issues/143]
